analysis: Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. Head lines 1494-1509 add a Qwen3-VL (qwen3_vl_moe) content-seed for the reasoning parser when the prompt tail has no think marker. Head lines 1556-1589 add a 'Streamed auto tool calls' section: incremental tool-call deltas for tool_choice=auto on gemma, qwen35, harmony and json formats, with a typed tool_choice violation if the final parse diverges after exposure, and a tool_call marker per fragment in the response hash. No code, keys, endpoints or deployment settings are changed here. Threat-model relevance: A-001 and TB-002/TB-007 (response path). The documented streaming behavior does not weaken the encryption path described in T-008, which concerns fail-closed SSE encryption. Fragments are emitted only after the function name resolves to a declared tool. Undeclared names are never exposed. Required/named tool_choice and native-channel families still release only validated complete calls. One residual point for integration: the doc says exposed fragments are validated against the complete parse only at frame close, so a divergent call can leak already-streamed argument bytes to the consumer before the typed error. That is the consumer's own response, not a cross-tenant exposure. The doc does not show whether the per-fragment hash markers, and therefore the receipt/billing response hash, stay consistent with the coordinator verifier (ProviderLoop+SSEParser.swift encodeToolCallsForHash). That code is not supplied, so I could not verify it. T-041 (prefix cache) is not touched. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the other claims in the second unit (MTP, sampling defaults, deadlines) appear unchanged context. No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
